facts.raw_span: stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma
metastases of the liver, lungs, and peritoneum
Photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption
Diffuse erythema of forehead and midface, involving nasolabial folds
Erythema and edema of upper eyelids
Creatine kinase: 1088 U/L
Antinuclear antibody titer: 1:640 with speckled pattern
Jo-1 antibody: negative
MRI showed mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers
Grade 4/5 strength on resisted abduction of shoulders bilaterally
Limited flexion of both hips

concepts.why: The patient's skin symptoms, including photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption, diffuse erythema of forehead and midface, and erythema of upper eyelids, along with muscle weakness and elevated creatine kinase levels, are consistent with dermatomyositis.
The patient developed skin symptoms and muscle weakness after starting ipilimumab treatment, which is a known side effect of this medication, suggesting ipilimumab-induced dermatomyositis.

The patient's muscle weakness, elevated creatine kinase levels, and muscle biopsy showing atrophy of type II muscle fibers are consistent with polymyositis, although the absence of inflammatory myositis on biopsy makes this diagnosis less likely.
The patient's antinuclear antibody titer and speckled pattern, along with muscle weakness and skin symptoms, suggest an overlap syndrome, although the specific diagnosis is unclear.
The patient's stage IV malignant melanoma and development of dermatomyositis suggest a paraneoplastic syndrome, although the exact relationship between the two conditions is unclear.
The negative Jo-1 antibody result does not rule out anti-synthetase syndrome, which can present with similar skin and muscle symptoms.

rationales.F01: Melanoma is associated with dermatomyositis, particularly in the context of C05.
rationales.F03: Photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption is a characteristic skin finding in dermatomyositis.
rationales.F06: Elevated creatine kinase levels are a hallmark of muscle inflammation in dermatomyositis and polymyositis.
rationales.F08: The absence of Jo-1 antibodies makes anti-synthetase syndrome less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient developed skin symptoms after starting ipilimumab treatment, and the symptoms recurred and worsened after a second course of ipilimumab, suggesting a strong association between the treatment and the symptoms.
